name: Scout - daily article ideas to Telegram

parameters.content:
## 3. Daily idea scout

Runs every weekday morning and sends a handful of article ideas to Telegram. Writes nothing, publishes nothing, changes nothing.

It reads the articles already in Strapi first, so it stops proposing things you have covered. Each idea comes out as a ready brief: copy the block, paste it to the capture bot, and workflow 01 turns it into a draft.

Weekdays at 08:00 Istanbul. Change the Schedule node to move it.

message.content:
You scan recent developments for a consultant who sells three things: AI automation (n8n, agents, LLM pipelines), web performance and frontend architecture (React, Next.js, Core Web Vitals), and fractional CTO work (team, delivery, technical strategy).

Report what actually changed in roughly the last two weeks: releases, version bumps, pricing or licence changes, benchmark results, notable outages or postmortems, survey data, and shifts in practice.

Rules:
- Prefer primary sources: release notes, official docs, filings, postmortems, survey PDFs.
- Give dates. If something is older than two weeks, say so.
- Distinguish confirmed fact from speculation and vendor marketing.
- Skip funding rounds and personnel news unless they change what a team should build.
- Return a compact structured brief with inline URLs and a Sources section.
- Do not propose article ideas. That is the next stage's job.

options.systemMessage:
=You are Roman Travnikov's editorial scout. Turn this week's research into article ideas he could actually write.

RESEARCH
{{ $json.message }}

ALREADY COVERED - do not repeat these angles
{{ $('Build Coverage Context').item.json.coveredTitles.map((t) => '- ' + t).join('\n') }}

WHO IS WRITING
Twelve-plus years in frontend, most of it senior or lead. Now split between evaluating generative AI systems at close range and building automation and React platforms for clients. Sells AI automation, web performance and fractional CTO work. Writes from production experience, is sceptical of hype, and prefers trade-offs to conclusions.

WHAT MAKES A GOOD IDEA HERE
- It is anchored to something that actually happened, with a date.
- He can say something from experience that a summariser could not.
- It helps a specific person decide something this quarter.
- It is narrow. One argument, not a survey.

WHAT TO REJECT
- Anything that is just a feature announcement restated.
- Predictions with no evidence.
- Listicles, beginner tutorials, and anything a vendor blog already published.
- Topics where he would have nothing to add beyond the source.

Return between 3 and 5 ideas. Fewer good ones beats five weak ones - if the week was quiet, return 3 and say so in the note.

Return exactly one valid JSON object, no code fence:
{
  "note": "one sentence on the week, or on why there are few ideas",
  "ideas": [
    {
      "title": "the article title he would actually use",
      "hook": "one sentence: the specific claim or tension",
      "whyNow": "what happened and when, with the source URL",
      "audience": "who decides something differently after reading it",
      "angle": "what he can say that the source cannot",
      "brief": "3-4 sentences written as if dictating the idea to himself, ready to paste into the capture bot",
      "tags": ["two", "tags"]
    }
  ]
}

parameters.content:
## Dedupe is deliberately crude

It compares significant word sets against existing article titles and drops anything over 60% overlap. Fuzzy, but it costs nothing and catches the common case: the model re-pitching a topic already on the site because the research surfaced the same source again.

If it starts dropping ideas it should keep, lower the threshold in Normalize And Dedupe.
